newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Guterres, Gonzalez see Iberia starting EMU.
newsitem.headline: Guterres, Gonzalez see Iberia starting EMU.

text.p: Portuguese Prime Minister Antonio Guterres and Spanish opposition leader Felipe Gonzalez said on Tuesday they were confident both their countries would qualify for Europe's single currency.

"I am profoundly convinced that Spain and Portugal are going to be part of the nucleus (of monetary union)," Guterres told journalists at the end of a one-day meeting between his Socialist party and its Spanish counterpart led by Gonzalez.
"And as head of the government, I am deeply determined to create the conditions for this to happen," he added.

Gonzalez, who led Spain for 13 years until he lost power in elections last spring, said that both Spain and Portugal were making the necessary effort to qualify for economic and monetary union (EMU) at its launch in January 1999.
This was done not just in terms of meeting the convergence criteria for the union but also in terms of assuring future stability, Gonzalez said.

European Union states will meet in the spring of next year to decide which countries qualify to launch the single currency on the basis of their having meet economic tests for entry laid down in the Maastricht Treaty.
Despite the economic problems faced by Germany, particularly with regard to its budget deficit, Gonzalez said that he was certain that Germany could make the grade.
"If it were not prepared (for entry), there will be no euro," he said, refering to the name of the future single currency.

During the meeting, attended by some 20 party officials from both countries, the Socialist parties discussed issues ranging from unemployment to negotiations to reform the European Union to prepare it for the entry of new members.
